GHSA-XVH5-G6GV-559V.570df030c0d30c2bf5336b2ab59f3902d8ab0b6d:
Validate TIFF tag values against libtiff's own field definition before TIFFSetField

PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew chose the TIFFSetField() argument shape
(scalar, tuple, or bytes) from the Python value alone, assuming its own
ImagingLibTiffMergeFieldInfo() registration would determine how libtiff
reads the varargs. It does not: TIFFMergeFieldInfo() never overrides
libtiff's built-in definition for a tag it already knows, so libtiff
reads the varargs according to its own field table regardless of what
Pillow pushed.

For a counted array tag such as DNGPrivateData (50740), a scalar
integer from the source file was taken by libtiff as a byte count, and
the data pointer was read from an argument slot Pillow never wrote --
copying that many bytes of process memory into the output tag. For a
fixed-size array tag such as ActiveArea (50829), the integer was used
directly as a source address, causing a segfault.

Add ImagingLibTiffFindField() to look up libtiff's actual field
definition (type, passcount, writecount) for a tag, and validate the
Python value against it before calling TIFFSetField, raising
ValueError instead of forwarding a mismatched value. The core tags that
have their own dedicated branches (ColorMap, YCbCrSubsampling,
ReferenceBlackWhite) are shape-checked too; ColorMap length is already
validated in Python. ReferenceBlackWhite no longer needs to be
blocklisted and is now written. TransferFunction remains unsupported by
the libtiff encoder and stays blocklisted, so it is still dropped.

Reported-by: carlini
Fixes: GHSA-xvh5-g6gv-559v

GHSA-VVXP-FM22-FCHW.ec5f1cbcf67275641abaad5c065ffb64a0a804a9:
Take libtiff scanline geometry tags from the image, not tiffinfo/exif

In TiffImagePlugin._save's libtiff branch, only BITSPERSAMPLE was
pinned to the real image's value when building the encoder's tag
list. IMAGEWIDTH, IMAGELENGTH and PLANAR_CONFIGURATION were set from
im.size but then overwritten by the tiffinfo=/exif= merge loop, and
SAMPLESPERPIXEL was never set at all for single-band modes, letting
a value from the caller's tags -- or from a re-saved source TIFF's
own IFD -- reach TIFFSetField unfiltered.

ImagingLibTiffEncode hands TIFFWriteScanline a row buffer sized from
the real image, with no check against libtiff's own scanline size
(computed from the tag-described geometry). Depending on which tag
was overridden, this let libtiff read (SamplesPerPixel/ImageWidth
too large) or, with Predictor=2, write (horizontal differencing
rewrites the scanline in place) past the end of that buffer.

Confirmed live on this build:
- Re-saving a JPEG with exif={SamplesPerPixel: 3, Photometric: RGB}
  via `im.save(out, "TIFF", exif=exif, compression="tiff_lzw")`: on
  the unfixed baseline, 80 of the 128 heap bytes trailing the row
  buffer leaked verbatim into the saved file's row 0. On the fixed
  build the real 1-sample-per-pixel geometry is used regardless of
  the supplied tags, so the (now self-inconsistent, Photometric=RGB
  but 1 sample) output is rejected as unreadable rather than leaking
  heap -- matching the reporter's documented expected outcome.
- Re-saving the same JPEG with an oversized ImageWidth tag: the
  unfixed baseline crashed with a bus error (this platform's
  equivalent of the report's SIGSEGV) trying to read a huge scanline
  out of a 64-byte buffer. The fixed build ignores the malicious
  width entirely (geometry always comes from the real image) and
  completes the save normally with exit code 0.

Fix (reporter's patch 1 of 2, chosen over the Python-only patch 2 for
defense in depth):
- src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py: pre-seed `atts` with SAMPLESPERPIXEL,
  IMAGEWIDTH, IMAGELENGTH and PLANAR_CONFIGURATION taken from the
  image being saved, alongside the existing BITSPERSAMPLE, so no
  tiffinfo/exif/source-IFD tag can override the geometry libtiff
  sizes its scanline from. This closes the tiffinfo=, exif= and
  re-saved-source-IFD routes alike, without touching the raw-writer
  behaviour relied on by test_tiff_chunks.
- src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c, ImagingLibTiffEncode: defense in depth
  -- reject any remaining configuration where TIFFScanlineSize64()
  exceeds the row buffer before the encode loop runs, raising
  IMAGING_CODEC_CONFIG instead of over-reading/over-writing. Reuses
  ImagingLibTiffEncodeCleanup() on both this new path and the
  existing TIFFWriteScanline error path so the TIFF handle is always
  closed before its buffer is freed (the same use-after-free class
  fixed for GHSA-vvxp-fm22-fchw).

Adds test_geometry_tags to Tests/test_file_libtiff.py, parametrised
over oversized IMAGEWIDTH/IMAGELENGTH, SAMPLESPERPIXEL=3 and
PLANAR_CONFIGURATION=2 via tiffinfo=.

Reported-by: carlini
Fixes: GHSA-xcvg-w56q-r89m

GHSA-332P-7HRC-92WF.78c08bd4d9c08037f77465a61d90633f669013f4:
Fix heap buffer overflow in _tiffWriteProc when saving TIFF to BytesIO

libtiff seeks past the current end of data when writing the directory
and writes tag values there. _tiffWriteProc sized its realloc() from
state->size + size instead of the write position state->loc + size,
so the first out-of-line tag value written after such a seek could
overrun the allocation by up to the size of the directory. The bytes
skipped by the seek were also never zeroed, leaking stale heap
contents into the saved file.

Size the buffer from the write position and zero the space added by
realloc, matching the semantics of writing to a real file. Reject
writes where the position is still beyond the buffer for the
non-reallocating case.

Reported-by: carlini
Reported-by: Tomer-PL
Fixes: GHSA-332p-7hrc-92wf

Fix DOS in PSDImagePlugin -- CVE-2021-28675

* PSDImagePlugin did not sanity check the number of input layers and
  vs the size of the data block, this could lead to a DOS on
  Image.open prior to Image.load.
* This issue dates to the PIL fork

CVE-2021-28676.bb6c11fb889e6c11b0ee122b828132ee763b5856:
Fix FLI DOS -- CVE-2021-28676

* FliDecode did not properly check that the block advance was
  non-zero, potentally leading to an infinite loop on load.
* This dates to the PIL Fork
* Found with oss-fuzz

CVE-2021-28677.5a5e6db0abf4e7a638fb1b3408c4e495a096cb92:
Fix EPS DOS on _open -- CVE-2021-28677

* The readline used in EPS has to deal with any combination of \r and
  \n as line endings. It used an accidentally quadratic method of
  accumulating lines while looking for a line ending.
* A malicious EPS file could use this to perform a DOS of Pillow in
  the open phase, before an image was accepted for opening.
* This dates to the PIL Fork
